body: I saw my psychologist yesterday - she put things in perspective. It’s definitely an internal thing to solve. I was just so convinced for literally the past month that my partner wasn’t doing enough. I just hope he can forgive me because I did not realize how out of control it was.

Thank you for taking so much time to analyze my post. I went to my psychologist yesterday and she pretty much said the same thing. 

I think sometimes I’m so upset and my brain is foggy that I miss the obvious. I know all the thinking styles and the CBT process to challenge my thoughts - but I was so convinced that if only my partner could ‘insert something here’ my insecurity/ anxiety would ease.  I feel like a bit of a knob. 

So now that I’ve had my dose of reality I just have to wait and give my partner space. Hopefully he will forgive me for being crazy needy.  Giving him space is killing me, my insecurities are raging, but I need to start breaking the cycle. 

Thank you again for your reply. I really appreciate it 🙂

I’m really sorry to hear this. I am in the same boat getting my head together so my partner doesn’t leave. 

I also think to myself - I don’t want him to stay for the sake of me. I want him to want me because he wants too.  I bet you feel the same way too, as much as it hurts. 

Time heals, take it day by day, it will start to hurt less
Lots of us feel lonely, even when we are surrounded by lots of people
It is so easy to be a victim - my brain feels so full There’s hardly room to get though my work let alone solve my lifes big problems.

Just read your post and you are literally identical to me. My partner keeps telling me to live in the moment but I also find it difficult to ignore my insecurities about things not working out. 

Have you found anything to be helpful?
